title: Asynchronous cooperative KV spill/prefetch for mixed tensor-pipeline parallel deployments
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Design and implement an asynchronous cooperative spill-and-prefetch protocol for KV cache shards across mixed tensor and pipeline parallel topologies. Objective is to reduce peak GPU memory pressure and tail latency for multi-GPU serving by enabling peers to proactively prefetch hot KV slices and to cooperatively spill cold slices to pinned CPU memory or NVMe with minimal blocking of inference micro-batches.
background: We see frequent OOMs and high tail latency on 8+ GPU pipeline deployments when KV working set exceeds per-GPU budgets. Existing approaches either evict aggressively (increasing token generation cost) or replicate KV slices (wasting memory). Previous tickets explored sharding and pipeline-aware striping (ENG-23890, ENG-19204), but we need a runtime-level cooperative mechanism that works with continuous batching and heterogeneous tensor/pipeline layouts.
goals: Reduce peak GPU memory used by KV cache by >= 25% on long-context workloads
Keep 99.9th percentile token latency within current SLO for steady-state continuous batching
Ensure correctness across tensor+pipeline parallel setups without global stalls
Provide metrics to reason about prefetch hit-rate, spill frequency, and cross-GPU bandwidth utilization
proposal_summary: Introduce a lightweight fractional-ownership protocol where each GPU advertises ownership confidence for KV slices; GPUs asynchronously spill low-confidence slices to pinned CPU pages and expose an RPC-driven prefetch window so upstream pipeline stages can fetch hot slices before they are needed. Prefetching happens out-of-band on dedicated I/O/p2p workers and is prioritized by a hotness score derived from recent access patterns and continuous-batching trace data.
technical_design: Ownership vector: per-slice float in [0,1] representing local hotness and availability; updated by access counters and decay window
Async spill: cold slices are serialized into pinned CPU pages (page-aligned) using a compact layout; spill writer uses a background CUDA stream + CPU thread to avoid blocking inference streams

Prefetch pipeline: when a micro-batch is scheduled, the router consults predicted token positions and issues prefetch requests for slices with ownership < threshold to GPUs that advertise them; prefetch uses GPU-GPU P2P via CUDA IPC where available, otherwise RDMA/PCIe pinned memcpy
Epoch tags: each KV slice carries a lightweight version tag to detect stale reads; tags increment on writes (e.g., prompt appends) and prefetch logic verifies tag before swapping into local cache

Non-blocking fallback: if prefetch misses or spool is busy, inference proceeds with a fallback on-demand fetch that may incur a short stall but is bounded by a per-request stall budget configurable per route
Eviction policy: hybrid LRU + hotness threshold within local shard; cooperative transfer avoids cross-shard double-eviction by reserving a tiny margin for in-flight prefetches

Integration with continuous batching: prefetch heuristics consume batched request traces to build short-horizon sequence prediction for upcoming KV keys, allowing proactive pre-warm of caches between micro-batches
Memory negotiation: GPUs periodically gossip their free-memory budgets and bandwidth headroom to tune ownership thresholds and prefetch concurrency to avoid saturating PCIe buses
Telemetry: lightweight counters for prefetch_hit, prefetch_miss, spill_rate, p2p_bytes, stall_ms by route/model/route-tag
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (prototype): implement ownership vector + CPU spill format + background spill worker; test with single pipeline stage locally
Phase 2 (prefetch): add RPC prefetch path and P2P transfers; integrate epoch tags and non-blocking fallback
Phase 3 (integration): wire into continuous-batching router; add memory gossip and prefetch concurrency tuning
Phase 4 (hardening): implement metrics, dashboards, and safety knobs (max spill rate, stall budget); run cluster canary and A/B experiments
PRs: runtime PR (rwd/runtime#1892), prefetch worker (rwd/runtime#1895), router integration (rwd/router#442)
milestones: 2026-02-25: Prototype spill worker + unit tests completed
2026-03-04: End-to-end prefetch P2P proof-of-concept on 4-GPU pod
2026-03-15: Canary rollout on dedicated infra for selected long-context routes
2026-03-29: Metrics dashboard and rollout to runtime-1.24
testing_and_metrics: Microbenchmarks: peak GPU memory vs baseline, prefetch hit-rate at 1s/10s windows
E2E: token generation p50/p95/p99 under continuous-batching at target QPS
Regression: correctness test verifying epoch tags prevent stale KV reads across pipeline restarts
Canary metrics: prefetch_miss rate < 5% and additional tail stall < 2ms per token or configurable per route
Cost: measure host CPU/NVMe usage for spills to ensure overhead < 8% of baseline infra cost
risks: P2P bandwidth saturation on busy clusters causing general perf regression
Complexity in ownership convergence leading to oscillations (aggressive prefetch then rapid eviction)
Edge cases with model writes (streaming generation with token appended during prefetch) requiring careful epoch management
Increased CPU/NVMe IO leading to contention with other services on shared hosts
